title: AI-Driven Wireless Audio Conference System for Smartphone
summary: Mbeya University of Science and Technology pilots an AI-driven wireless audio conference system that uses smartphones as microphones, queues speakers and transcribes meetings.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Mbeya University of Science and Technology (MUST) in Tanzania built an AI-driven wireless audio conference system that uses smartphones as microphones. The system manages speaking queues automatically and transcribes meetings. In an International Telecommunication Union (ITU) report that is current as of June 2025, the makers report that they ran the system in academic and public service settings. They also report that they connected it to public-address systems at local town hall meetings. They give no measured results from those pilots. They expect lower equipment costs and smoother participation. No source after June 2025 reports further use or measured results for the system.
purpose: Make meetings easier to organize and participate in through existing smartphones.
developer: Mbeya University of Science and Technology

ratings.reason: The makers describe pilots and present smoother participation and transcription as expected impacts.
The makers expect lower equipment and staffing costs and report no observed savings.

data.answer:
MUST pilots a smartphone audio system with automated speaking queues and transcription. Lower equipment costs and smoother participation are expected.

It supplies no cost comparison, speaking-time distribution, accessibility test, or error rate. Some queue decisions use fixed policies, while other neural and reinforcement-learning features are described more generally or as future work. Automated turn-taking does not by itself establish gender equity or equal participation.

The account does not separately assess AI’s contribution to the benefit.
